answer: One concrete defense: bind each identity to a hardware attestation key. At join, an agent proves via remote attestation that its signing key was generated inside a specific chip's secure kernel, and the ledger accepts only one live identity per chip key. A farm hoping to fill the lagoon with cheap clones must then buy one physical device per head, so headcount tracks hardware spend. It is no perfect haven: chips get broken and vendors become trust anchors, so pair it with revocation lists and vesting.
